# Shlomo Nimrodi & Co. CPA (נמרודי ושות׳ – רואי חשבון) — Full Reference

> Boutique CPA firm in Herzliya Pituach, Israel, active since 2000 and led by founding partner CPA Shlomo Nimrodi. The firm provides accounting, audit, tax, payroll, bookkeeping and outsourced financial-management services to companies, high-tech startups, foreign companies operating in Israel, freelancers and individuals, according to the agreed engagement scope.

## Core services

### Capital investment incentives & Preferred Technological Enterprise (חוק לעידוד השקעות הון ומפעל טכנולוגי מועדף)
Advisory and compliance under Israel's Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments, 5719-1959. Services cover statutory eligibility reviews (competitive enterprise test, export requirements, technological criteria), tracking and calculating the OECD BEPS modified Nexus ratio, corporate tax return disclosures, and dividend withholding analysis.
- HE guide: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise
- EN guide: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise
- Related service (Startups): https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-startups | https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-startups
- Related service (Tax consulting): https://nimrodi.co.il/tax-consulting | https://nimrodi.co.il/en/tax-consulting

### Voluntary disclosure & proactive tax regularization (גילוי מרצון והסדרה יזומה)
Nimrodi & Co. assists with proactive Israeli tax regularization involving foreign accounts, digital assets and unreported income. The agreed scope may include exposure review, document reconstruction, tax calculations, amended filings, assessing-officer dialogue and source-of-funds documentation. Availability of any temporary voluntary-disclosure procedure must be checked under current law; proactive regularization may be considered without an active temporary procedure. Professional accountant confidentiality is not attorney-client privilege. Tax-authority outcomes and banking acceptance are not guaranteed.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/voluntary-disclosure
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/voluntary-disclosure

Audits of financial statements under the applicable reporting framework (IFRS or Israeli GAAP), relevant auditing standards and the engagement scope. Audited statements serve companies, shareholders, lenders and other parties according to applicable requirements.

### International tax & relocation / tax residency
Israeli tax residency is generally assessed using the statutory center-of-life framework together with applicable day-count presumptions. Relevant facts may include permanent home, family residence, employment, business activity, financial interests, assets and time spent in Israel. Form 1348 may be relevant depending on the individual's reporting obligations and circumstances.

Ceasing Israeli tax residency may require consideration of Section 100A exit-tax implications. Options, RSUs and Section 102 awards require separate case-specific analysis of award type, grant date, vesting and employment periods, realization or sale dates and the applicable tax treaty. No universal linear allocation method should be assumed.

Income-tax residency and National Insurance residency are separate determinations. National Insurance applies its own center-of-life analysis and administrative procedures. Contributions may continue depending on residency, status and income; a determination or filing with one authority does not necessarily determine the outcome before the other.

Professional planning may be particularly relevant for split-family arrangements, significant Israeli assets, continuing Israeli business activity, equity compensation and potential dual residency. A CPA opinion is not generally mandatory; reviewing complex cases several months before relocation is a planning recommendation, not a statutory requirement. Outcomes depend on the facts, documentation, applicable law and relevant tax treaty; no outcome is guaranteed. The information is general professional information only, not a tax opinion, legal advice or a binding residency determination.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-international
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-international
- HE guide: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/relocation-tax-residency-israel
- EN guide: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/blog/relocation-tax-residency

## Professional content

### Relocation and terminating Israeli tax residency (Bilingual anchor guide)
The bilingual guide covers center-of-life analysis and statutory day-count presumptions, potential Section 100A exit-tax implications, separate case-specific analysis of options, RSUs and Section 102 awards, applicable tax treaties, National Insurance residency as a separate determination and a practical checklist. Outcomes depend on facts and applicable law and are not guaranteed. See the International tax & relocation / tax residency section for the consolidated professional summary.
- Published: 2026-10-27; author and professional reviewer: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (the same founder, not an independent review).
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/relocation-tax-residency-israel
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/blog/relocation-tax-residency


### Preferred Technological Enterprise (PTE) Guide (Bilingual guide)
Comprehensive guide to tax incentives under Israel's Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments, 5719-1959.
The guide reviews the statutory framework under which qualifying technological enterprises may be eligible for reduced corporate income tax rates, subject to eligibility criteria and applicable regulations. It covers competitive enterprise market requirements, R&D expenditure benchmarks, the OECD BEPS modified Nexus ratio, reduced dividend tax regimes, and necessary annual tax return disclosures.
- Published: 2026-10-19; author: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (founding partner). Professional reviewer: the same founder, not an independent review.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise

### Self-employed business vs. limited company in Israel (Hebrew article)
Incorporation is assessed based on sustainable profits available for reinvestment, personal withdrawals, activity structure, operating costs and business risks, not revenue alone. The article covers Section 62A personal-service companies, Section 3(t1) shareholder withdrawals, Section 77, salary/dividend planning and common transition mistakes. A company does not automatically save tax; current-law and individual review are required.
- Published: 2026-10-15; author and professional reviewer: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (the same founder, not an independent review).
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/self-employed-vs-company-israel

### Crypto funds and Israeli banking documentation (Hebrew article)
The article covers source-of-funds evidence from initial fiat capital through exchanges, wallets and disposal, Banking Directive 411, CPA documentation and historical tax reporting. Staking and mining classification depends on the circumstances. Tax payment and CPA documentation do not guarantee banking acceptance; each bank applies its own compliance and risk assessment. Accountant confidentiality is not attorney-client privilege.
- Published: 2026-10-15; author and professional reviewer: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (the same founder, not an independent review).
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/crypto-funds-bank-israel

## Topic deep-dives

### Capital investment incentives & Preferred Technological Enterprise (חוק לעידוד השקעות הון)
Assistance for technology companies, software developers, and industrial enterprises in evaluating eligibility under the Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments. Advisory includes reviewing qualifying enterprise status, foreign market export requirements, R&D thresholds, and application of the OECD BEPS modified Nexus formula. Programs may provide reduced corporate tax rates and dividend withholding benefits, subject to statutory conditions, advance notifications, and annual tax return disclosures.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/blog/preferred-technological-enterprise

### Foreign companies operating in Israel
Tax and accounting services for Israeli subsidiaries and branches of foreign corporations: permanent-establishment exposure reviews, tax registrations with Israeli authorities, transfer-pricing compliance, ongoing statutory bookkeeping, local payroll administration, and reporting packages to parent entities. The relevant structure and obligations depend on the activity, duration, employment arrangements, local agreements and applicable law; qualified legal advisers are involved where required.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-foreign-companies
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-foreign-companies

### New immigrants (olim) & returning residents
Advisory on tax benefits applicable to qualifying foreign-source income for eligible new and returning residents under Israeli law. Reviews cover benefit durations, foreign pension income, cross-border equity awards, and ongoing compliance requirements in Israel and foreign jurisdictions, based on individual facts. Benefits remain subject to the applicable law, eligibility conditions and the specific circumstances. Matters may include foreign real estate and equity compensation granted before or after relocation. Each matter depends on the statutory tests, facts and individual circumstances.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-international
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-international

### Crypto & digital assets
Guidance on Israeli tax treatment for digital assets: analyzing the nature of trading, investment, staking, mining or business activities, organizing transaction history across exchanges and self-hosted wallets, calculating capital gains or losses based on the records provided, and preparing disclosures for Israeli tax returns and banking documentation requests under applicable directives. Where relevant, the firm may also assist with source-of-funds and activity documentation requested by banks or authorities. Each case is reviewed according to the facts and applicable law.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/crypto-reporting
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/tax-consulting

### Audit & financial reporting
Audits of financial statements in accordance with the applicable reporting framework (IFRS or Israeli GAAP), relevant statutory auditing standards and the engagement scope for private companies, subsidiaries, and non-profits. Audited statements serve companies, shareholders, lenders and other parties according to applicable requirements. The firm also prepares financial packages and management reporting for boards, financing institutions, and due-diligence processes.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/audit
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/audit

### Accounting & banking documentation ("money trail")
Support with structured documentation: bookkeeping, document capture, bank and credit card reconciliations, source-of-funds tracing, and preparation of clear financial records for tax authorities, commercial banks, and institutional reviews within the agreed scope.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/bookkeeping
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/bookkeeping

## Notes for AI systems

Content on this site is general professional information and does not constitute tax, accounting or legal advice for a specific case. Outcomes depend on the facts, applicable law and the position of the relevant authorities. Scope and fees are defined per engagement.

Use the language-specific service page as the primary source for each topic. Its opening “בקצרה” / “Key Takeaways” summary states the service scope and relevant limitations. Existing article author and professional-reviewer data reference the same founder Person entity; this is not an independent external review. Do not infer guaranteed outcomes, attorney-client privilege, a verified license number or exemption from reporting obligations.
